dedupe_keys.name: new zealand national minimum dataset hospital events public and private hospital discharges with diagnoses and procedures with a public web tool

description: The National Minimum Dataset for hospital events is New Zealand's record of every stay in a public hospital and every publicly funded stay in a private one, the basis for national statistics on hospital use. It is held by Health New Zealand Te Whatu Ora, which collects coded discharge records from hospitals in an agreed electronic format. Coverage runs from 1993 for public hospitals, with records backloaded to 1988, and from 1997 for publicly funded private events. Each unit record carries a National Health Index number, admission and discharge details, diagnoses and procedures, and the data dictionary documents fields that have changed over time. Summaries are available free through a public web tool, updated every year, that breaks hospitalisations down by year, ethnicity, sex, district of residence, age, diagnosis and procedure, with detailed tables for the latest year; unit-record data are not a direct download and need an approved request. Caveats: coding and fields have changed several times, privately funded private hospital care is outside scope, and the web tool offers only summaries. Simulation uses: setting admission rates and length-of-stay distributions by district for hospital capacity and demand models. Related records: the New Zealand Trauma Registry (data-nz-trauma-registry) covers major trauma patients in more depth, and the HQSC quality data (data-hqsc-health-system-quality-dashboard-and-atlas) give quality indicators drawn partly from these records.
